Avenidas Novas — Lisbon, Portugal

Relatively safer day Average night

In detail

Coverage is more limited than in most neighbouring freguesias: a local outlet reported a spate of "violent assaults" alarming residents in September 2024, and a residents' petition circulated over a perceived rise in assaults; a residential burglary was intercepted by PSP one night in August 2023. In Lisbon's 2024/2025 parish-by-parish security survey, the Avenidas Novas junta did not respond, leaving official comment thin. No specific daytime safety concerns were found in current press coverage. Sources checked: Fregues.pt, 2 Sep 2024 – "Assaltos violentos nas Avenidas Novas ameaçam moradores"; Petição Pública – "Aumento de assaltos nas Avenidas Novas"; Notícias ao Minuto, 14 Aug 2023 – "Furtam residência após escalarem e arrombarem janela em Lisboa" (Avenidas Novas); Observador, special report (2024/2025 series) – "Insegurança em Lisboa ou mera perceção?" (Avenidas Novas junta did not respond).

Frequently asked questions

Is Avenidas Novas safe?

Wandroz currently rates Avenidas Novas in Lisbon, Portugal as relatively safer than most other areas covered on Wandroz during the day and roughly average compared to other areas covered on Wandroz at night. This is a qualitative first-pass assessment based on general local knowledge and public reputation, not an official geolocated crime dataset — see the note on data limitations below before treating it as more precise than it is.

At night, Avenidas Novas is rated as roughly average compared to other areas covered on Wandroz. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.
